verdict.rationale: Zero is an open-source AI email client that works on top of Gmail and other providers, so masked addresses or aliases are a fair question for this kind of product. Nothing in the evidence documents any alias, masked-address, or address-forwarding feature. Its general claim that it does not track or sell data is a different privacy capability and does not hide the user's real address from sign-ups or strangers.

support.subject: As a switcher, I can use aliases or masked addresses so sign-ups and strangers never learn my real address
